input.quote: a. Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: Section 5(a) imposes an unconditional minimum monthly fee for both Hosting Services and Support Services, irrespective of Client's actual usage, and Section 6 expressly strips Client of any right to supporting documentation or to contest those minimum fees. Nothing narrows the minimums to the current term (Section 13 renews the Agreement automatically for successive one-year periods carrying the same minimums), gives Client any right to reduce them on notice, or converts a shortfall into a true-up; Section 14's termination-on-notice right is itself made "Subject to Section 4," whose open-ended "not less than ____ months" Support Services period could extend the lock-in beyond twelve months. That fails the fallback on its material terms, so we have added a short proviso limiting the minimums to the current 12-month term, allowing Client to reduce them on 30 days' written notice, and requiring any shortfall to be trued up rather than penalised. We have left the fee floor itself in place rather than deleting it (our preferred position), which would require collateral edits to the Section 6 carve-outs.

ops.text: The minimum monthly fees set forth in Section 5(a) apply only during the current 12-month term, may be reduced by Client upon 30 days' written notice, and any shortfall against such minimums will be trued up rather than charged as a penalty.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept an unconditional minimum monthly fee. Consistent with our fallback position, we have limited the minimums to the current 12-month term, made them reducible by us on 30 days' notice, and provided that any shortfall is trued up rather than charged as a penalty.
proposal.summary: Add a proviso limiting the minimum monthly fees to the current 12-month term, allowing Client to reduce them on 30 days' notice, and requiring a true-up rather than a penalty for any shortfall.
